architecturalRedesign.summary: Heading recognition is redesigned around compositional, non-lexical evidence rather than any single hard-required signal, per this phase's explicit anti-special-casing charter. No phrase list of any kind was added anywhere. Each of the 4 findings was traced to a general, root-cause mechanism gap - not patched as an isolated case.

mechanisms.name: ciKeyword - capitalization as evidence, not a hard gate
mechanisms.whatChanged: ARTICLE_PATTERNS[0], SECTION_PATTERNS[0], and INTEGER_SECTION_PATTERNS[0] previously required the LITERAL keyword spelling ('ARTICLE'/'Section'/'SECTION', no `i` flag) - only the line-anchored fallback patterns carried `i`. `ciKeyword(word)` builds a per-letter case-insensitive alternation (e.g. '[Ss][Ee][Cc][Tt][Ii][Oo][Nn]') and is substituted for the literal keyword string in all three shape-based patterns.
mechanisms.whyThisIsGeneral: The whole-regex `i` flag was deliberately NOT used, because it would also relax the TITLE-shape character classes ([A-Z] for a SECTION title's first letter, [A-Z ,&';-] for an ARTICLE's ALL-CAPS title run) - the very capitalization evidence that distinguishes a genuine heading-shaped title from an ordinary lowercase sentence continuation. `ciKeyword` isolates case-insensitivity to exactly the one signal that carries no real evidentiary weight (a fixed keyword's own spelling case is typographic/OCR noise, not proof of anything) while leaving the title's own capitalization - genuine positive evidence - fully intact. This is the literal embodiment of the phase charter's own instruction: 'capitalization treated as evidence, not hard requirement.'
mechanisms.closesFinding: Category 'inconsistent capitalization' (lowercase 'section'/'article' keyword, mid-sentence, invisible on a continuous-prose document).

mechanisms.name: stripTrailingTypographicNoise - a real typographic-noise CLASS, not enumerated literal strings
mechanisms.whatChanged: `stripTrailingPageNumberArtifact` gained an `i` flag (its label regex has no OTHER case-sensitive character class, so `i` alone is the fully general fix - no companion workaround needed). A new `stripTrailingFootnoteMarker` function recognizes a short (1-3 digit) run glued DIRECTLY - no intervening whitespace - onto real sentence-terminal punctuation, as the general shape a superscript footnote/endnote marker collapses to under plain-text PDF extraction. Both are composed into one pipeline, `stripTrailingTypographicNoise`, applied uniformly to BOTH positional signals (A: paragraph break: B: sentence-terminal punctuation) and to BOTH SECTION and ARTICLE candidates, BEFORE either signal is ever evaluated.
mechanisms.whyThisIsGeneral: Adding a new noise class in the future means adding one more general strip function to the pipeline - never a per-document or per-phrase special case - and it automatically, uniformly protects every downstream consumer. The footnote-marker recognizer requires NO intervening whitespace between the punctuation and the digit run, which is exactly what makes it a purely typographic (never content-based) signal: a real inline citation number is always space-separated from its own keyword ('Section 6.05'), and a dollar figure's trailing digit group is comma-grouped, never a bare 1-3 digit stray glued to punctuation - so this cannot misfire on ordinary prose numerals.
mechanisms.criticalPrecisionGuard: The footnote-marker regex uses a `(?<!\d)` negative lookbehind on the punctuation character. WITHOUT this guard, a first draft of the fix silently misidentified an ORDINARY DECIMAL NUMBER ending a real sentence ('...shall not exceed 4.00 to 1.00') as 'terminal punctuation (the decimal point in 1.00) plus a glued footnote digit (00)', manufacturing a false sentence-end signal and reopening the already-certified Category 6 precision boundary (structural-heading-rx-adversarial-expansion.test.ts, describe block 6 - a numeric table row followed by the next section number must NOT become a heading). Caught empirically by re-running that exact test file after the first draft; fixed with the lookbehind; re-verified passing. Documented here because it is direct, load-bearing evidence that 'a heading whose removal would orphan a real child should weigh against dropping it' cuts both ways - a naive generalization that RECOVERS more headings can just as easily REOPEN a precision hole, and both directions were checked empirically, not assumed.
mechanisms.closesFinding: Categories 'footnote marker' (SECTION and ARTICLE alike) and 'ALL-CAPS page-artifact label'.
mechanisms.rankStackCorruptionPreventionIsRootCause: The ARTICLE case's real rank-stack corruption (its child SECTION silently re-parented to parentSectionRef=null) is prevented BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a separate rank-stack patch layered on top: once the noise hiding the ARTICLE's own real positional evidence is discounted BEFORE either signal is evaluated, the ARTICLE is never dropped in the first place, so there is nothing left to re-parent incorrectly. This directly satisfies the phase charter's 'a heading whose removal would orphan a real child should weigh against dropping it' via the stronger form of that requirement: removing the ROOT CAUSE of the wrongful drop, rather than adding a second, independent check to catch the consequence after the fact.

mechanisms.name: BOUNDED_GAP - a directly-coupled, pre-existing latent defect fixed at its root
mechanisms.whatChanged: ARTICLE_PATTERNS[0]'s (and, for the same general reason, SECTION_PATTERNS[0]'s and INTEGER_SECTION_PATTERNS[0]'s) number-to-title whitespace gap was a bare, UNBOUNDED `\s+`, able to span an entire real paragraph break (2+ newlines). `BOUNDED_GAP` restricts this specific gap to same-line whitespace or at most ONE newline - matching how every real heading's own number and title actually sit relative to each other in every real fixture (same line, or two immediately adjacent lines; never separated by a genuine blank line).
mechanisms.howThisWasDiscovered: NOT found by adversarial construction - surfaced as a real test regression while empirically verifying the `ciKeyword` fix. structural-heading-positive-evidence-false-negative-guard.test.ts's own 'repeated section label across two different ARTICLEs' case uses a Title-Case in-prose citation ('for Article I.') immediately before a real, distinct 'ARTICLE II COVENANTS' heading; making the ARTICLE keyword case-insensitive newly let that citation's own keyword match, and the pattern's unbounded gap then let its non-greedy title capture skip straight past the real paragraph break and swallow the entire, unrelated 'ARTICLE II COVENANTS' heading as if it were the citation's own title - silently deleting the real ARTICLE II occurrence from the index.
mechanisms.confirmedPreExisting: Verified via direct regex probing (not assumed) that this reproduces IDENTICALLY against the ORIGINAL, unmodified, purely case-sensitive pattern when the citation is written in ALL CAPS ('ARTICLE I.' instead of 'Article I.') - this is a genuine, pre-existing latent defect in the gap's own unboundedness, orthogonal to keyword case, that no existing committed test had ever exercised (every prior test's own citation-shaped ARTICLE reference happened to use Title Case, which the literal-'ARTICLE'-only pattern could not match at all, accidentally dodging the bug rather than avoiding it by design).
mechanisms.whyFixedHereRatherThanFiledSeparately: Directly coupled to this remediation's own scope per the phase's own antiEndlessLoopScopeBoundary rule ('directly-coupled consequences discovered during their own fix ... fixed only if necessary to close one of the 8'): it is the same file, the same pattern, the same 'does this candidate reach the plausibility gate as a well-formed match at all' question, and if left unfixed it produces exactly this module's own named failure class (a real heading silently vanishing) as a direct, mechanical side effect of legitimately fixing FINDING-1's own keyword-case gap. Recorded here as COUPLED-NEW per the phase's own terminology.
mechanisms.generalityCheck: Applied uniformly to all three keyword-anchored patterns with an analogous number-to-title gap, not only ARTICLE_PATTERNS[0] where it was discovered - the same general principle at every call site with the same shape.

findingByFinding.evidence: tests/certification/part-b-recert-blocker1-independent-adversarial.test.ts describe block 3, UNCHANGED assertion (heading still correctly not recovered) plus a NEW second test in the same block that is the concrete proof of the claim: the most obvious general candidate fix (accept a heading via strict sequential section-numbering continuity, e.g. this candidate's number is exactly the immediately-prior accepted section's number + 1, combined with 'at least one newline present') was constructed, and directly, empirically verified to ALSO accept structural-heading-rx-adversarial-expansion.test.ts's own already-certified Category 6 false-positive case ('Section 5.01 ... \nSection 5.02 ...' - a numeric table row with no terminal punctuation, single newline, sequential-by-one numbering - required by that test's own assertion to NOT become a heading). Both defect 3's own shape and Category 6's own shape reduce to the identical, indistinguishable typographic signature: prior line ends in ordinary content (no terminal punctuation), exactly one newline, next candidate's number is the immediate successor. No positional, paragraph-geometry, or numbering-sequence evidence available to this design tells the two apart, so no general fix exists that recovers one without also recovering the other - and the other is a real, tested, deliberately-preserved boundary this phase's charter (and Workstream A's own prior RX pass) already examined and correctly refused to cross. Treated as the SAME boundary re-confirmed under a new name, not a fourth independent defect, consistent with the phase's own 'antiEndlessLoopScopeBoundary' instruction not to re-litigate already-certified boundaries.

commits.summary: Production fix: ciKeyword, stripTrailingTypographicNoise (page-number `i` flag + new footnote-marker stripping), BOUNDED_GAP - lib/contract-model/compiler/stage-structure.ts only.

overallSummary: FINDING-1 (structural heading false negatives): 3 of the 4 findings Part B's own recertification reported are FIXED GENERALLY via a redesigned, compositional heading-recognition mechanism (ciKeyword for capitalization-as-evidence; stripTrailingTypographicNoise for a real typographic-noise class covering both the footnote-marker and ALL-CAPS-page-label gaps and preventing the associated rank-stack corruption by construction, at its root, rather than patching the symptom). One directly-coupled, pre-existing latent defect (BOUNDED_GAP) was discovered and fixed along the way, per the phase's own COUPLED-NEW provision. The 4th finding (multi-column-layout collapse) is confirmed, with concrete counter-test evidence rather than assumption, to be the SAME already-examined precision boundary as the existing, deliberately-preserved Category 6 case - no general fix exists that recovers it without reopening a real, certified false-positive regression, so it is left unchanged and clearly documented rather than papered over. All 7 originally-certified real-fixture anomaly sites remain independently re-verified at 0 against the real CONMED/DSGR fixtures. No package-specific tuning anywhere in the production fix. Zero regressions across 123 structural-heading-suite tests, tsc, and eslint for this workstream's own files.
